minutes.headline: Water commissioners approved the bond issue for the Massachusetts Avenue water main replacement and heard PFAS pilot results.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District commissioners heard consultants report on pilot testing of PFAS treatment at the Hickory Hills and Lancaster Ave wells. They agreed to let counsel respond to an open meeting law complaint and approved the bond details for the water main replacement project. The board also discussed a Pleasant Street main break and complaints about communication, a possible cell equipment pod on a water tank, meter-reading costs, and a leak detection grant.

public_comment.stated_role: water user and resident (said he lives on Green Court)
public_comment.topic: Asked why water district funds are being used for a site survey at the closed Hickory Hills well; the chair said the district's counsel is directing communication through attorneys because of correspondence from the Woodlands association's lawyer.
Suggested notifying the fire chief and dispatch about water main breaks; the superintendent said dispatch already knows but communication between dispatchers is limited.

votes.motion: Accept the minutes of the prior district meeting (the date was stated as January 8th).
Allow KP Law to move forward with the response to the open meeting law complaint as written.
Approve the details of the bond issue for the Massachusetts Avenue water main replacement as they appear in the votes prepared by bond counsel, to be put into the minutes.

budget_items.topic: General obligation bond, water main replacement project
budget_items.what_was_said: Six bids came in for the bond and Raymond James and Associates was the low bidder. Debt service is roughly level each year for 20 years, with the first payment due in the 2025 date stated.

budget_items.topic: Customer bill effect of the bond
budget_items.what_was_said: Staff expect the dedicated line item on bills to fall from the current charge to a lower quarterly figure. Money collected on that line goes only to this project.

The consultant's cost analysis found the newer clay media less expensive over time than carbon because it lasts longer, though carbon vessels offer more flexibility. Annualized media costs and replacement intervals were shown in a report table.

budget_items.topic: State funding application for PFAS treatment
budget_items.what_was_said: The board needs cost information before applying for state funding. Applications were due late July last year and the funding is expected to run out. A $50 million package was floated as a question.

budget_items.topic: Meter reading software for deduct meters
budget_items.what_was_said: The billing vendor's verbal estimate for programming the deduct reads is an annual fee. The clerk treasurer suggested sewer should pay for the deduct part.
A grant would cover leak detection equipment and a leak survey, due at the end of the month. A leak survey alone was said to cost much less than the grant.

decisions.decision: Board leaned toward waiting for the Kings pilot study results, meeting early to review a data summary, and meeting DEP informally before any funding application.
Board asked the consultant for a spreadsheet of construction and maintenance costs for each treatment option, including a combined plant.
The superintendent will ask the engineering firm for a design quote for a pod to hold cellular equipment on the Sunny Hill Road tank; any contract would come back to the board for a vote.
Staff will pursue the leak detection grant application and bring the meter-reading fee issue back at the next meeting.

what_happened.line: Commissioners moved to approve the bond details for the Massachusetts Avenue water main replacement; the vote outcome was not audible, though ayes were heard.
Six bids came in for the bond; Raymond James and Associates was the low bidder, with debt service roughly level over 20 years.
Consultants presented PFAS pilot results for the Hickory Hills and Lancaster Ave wells; the board leaned toward waiting for the Kings pilot study before applying for funding.
A motion to let KP Law respond to the open meeting law complaint as written was made; the outcome was not audible.
Staff will pursue a leak detection grant and bring the meter-reading fee issue back at the next meeting; a design quote for a cell equipment pod will be requested.

why_it_matters: The bond sets the debt payments behind the dedicated line on water bills for the water main project, and staff expect that line to fall to a lower quarterly figure.
PFAS treatment is likely to be a large future cost for water customers, and the choice of treatment media and the timing of a state funding application will shape how much of it the district carries.
The meter-reading fee for deduct meters is unresolved, including whether sewer should pay for part of it, so a charge could reach some customers' bills.
